Water from Christ’s side moderates the way to paradise and extinguishes the fire of hell, 123. It washes away the record of debt. Water is the drink of penitents, 137. Christ enters the water of the Jordan to wash away the sin of the world, 160. How the Lord’s voice is over the waters. Why the Holy Spirit floats upon the waters in the form of a dove. Why the water is to be changed into the mystery of blood, 160. It presses upon fire, and flame multiplies the wave, 164. It is offered by the hands of a host to one coming to table, 171. How external water can cleanse hearts. Burning water is inflamed by streams, and increases the burning of the one who drinks, 172.

The divine eagle protects us with the wings of wisdom, 170.

When the north wind caused the shipwreck of the whole world, 20.

How human free choice was held captive by sin, 114. When it obeys the Gospel, it is the benefit of the one who calls. We must pray that ours may be governed by God, 67.

The tree. The seductive tree, when opened, closed the eyes, 99. The tree’s taste had infected the mouths. The mustard tree is for healing. The unfruitful tree is to be replaced, 106. The barren tree is hostile to fruitful branches. After the Gospel the unfruitful tree will be cut down. It is wholly present in the seed, 111. A defect in the seed is a defect in the whole tree. The tree that is completely white in blossom in spring does not bear fruit, 162. It disperses harmful things at the roots and destroys the joined monuments of the ancestors, 162. Human beings appeared as walking trees to the blind man who had been enlightened, 176. Trees are born in time and vanish with time. See Root, Appearance.

The ruler of the synagogue. Why he asks Christ to lay His hand upon his daughter, 33. He gives the woman with the hemorrhage a way of reaching Christ, 34. What he can learn from her. Why he is foolish. He meets the Lord, and what he does, 36. He is the father of the synagogue. And how. Why his daughter was twelve years old. When his daughter is raised by Christ, 63. They are indignant that Christ heals on the sabbaths, 105.

To rebuke criminals is to incur hatred, 127.

Weapons turned toward luxury, 27.

When arrogance ceases in a rich and powerful man, he himself is blessed, 136.

Art comes to nature’s aid in perfecting a work, 132. Even in a newly born human being one must not seek by art what cannot be found by art, 160. Where it heals, there the weariness of illness comes to rest, 18.

Nautical art. See Sailor.

To ascend. The higher someone ascends, the higher he falls, 26. Christ ascends the cross, 58 and 144.

A seductive appearance struck down the woman; a saving appearance raised her up, 74. It is obscured by smoke. The tree stained the woman’s eyes; Christ’s tomb cleanses them, 77. Appearance alone does not make judgment concerning things secure, 145. The human being cannot grasp God, 147.

Astrology wavers in conjectures, deceives by its art, posits fate, gathers numbers, and other things, etc., 156. The astrologer would not have found the King of heaven unless God had revealed Him. He errs along with the wandering stars, 160. It is condemned because, while looking intently at the stars, it neglects salvation, 164. See “Notes,” in sermon 157.

What it means to attend to oneself, 139. He attends to himself who attends to another. Blessed is the one who attends to himself and to his neighbor, 155.

Avarice is avoided through almsgiving, 7. It arises from wealth. Its likeness is fasting without mercy, 8. The devil recommends it during Lent, 13. Through it gold becomes heavier, 29. It must be trampled underfoot, 54. Its rage is softened, 104. Whoever flees the light of mercy surrenders himself to its darkness. It generates scarcity. It is recognized through gold, 116. Through it a person stores up many things for others, to his own torment, 122. It denies parents, and so forth. It is the root of all evils, and how, 162. It is the school of impiety, 30.

The avaricious person is envious, 4. He calculates as lost what another possesses. How the one who preserves his substance loses it, 7. He is rich in punishment, not in wealth, 22. A guardian of what belongs to others. He is punished in the other age. How Christ satisfies his greed, 25. What generosity means to him, 28. His evils, 30. A guardian of what belongs to others, not master of what is his own, 42. The avaricious person reduces himself into the purse. He is a slave of riches, and how he can trample avarice underfoot, 54. He abandons what belongs to the future life, 114. He accuses gold, 116. Always seeking, he does not always possess, 104.

The author of evil. If he is extinguished, evil is worth nothing, 11. Whoever tramples upon the author of enmities despises the enmities themselves, 14.

The authority of the one who commands removes presumption from the one who speaks, 70. The authority of the speaker is emptied by insults, 131.

The hearer receives from the teacher what he deserves, 86. The hearer’s mind must not be kept in suspense for long, 88. Let him ask God for the desire to hear, 96. The minds of the hearers are suspended by Christ, 99. The affairs of the world are kept silent because we do not hear them in the proper manner, 101. He becomes weary from repeated reading, 120. [Col. 1147] From weariness, 122. He hears properly when the powers of the mind have been restored. Whoever has decided to err hears what he wants, not what is, 131. To what he should be exhorted so that he may hear with fruit, 136. What the rash hearer of God’s word does, 156. What happens to a bad hearer, 158. Where he is not present, shouting is useless, 167. How the hearer of God’s word should adapt himself to the preacher, 173.

Our hearing is burdened by a long discourse, 96. To be perfect, it must belong both to mind and body, 61. Bad hearing removes good sight, 78. Understanding of the Scriptures must be moderated by the most devout hearing, 126. Why God imputes known things as though they had been heard, 125. Not knowing what has been heard is a torment, 132.

Countless filthy birds compared with one dove, 171. The spears of crimes must be driven from hearts by the cross. Birds are demons flying through the air, 29.

Gold must be carried from the depths of the earth to the dwelling of the soul, 22. It has a tomb. It is heavy, but through avarice it becomes heavier, 29. The nature and evil effects of gold at length. The one salvation is to send gold to heaven through the hands of the poor. The evils of gold are shown by examples. It destroys human conduct, nature, and God. Wherever there is a rich vein of gold, all skill is expended in possessing it, 91. Gold is not avarice, but avarice is recognized through it, 116. It lies hidden in the earth, 139. It is owed to the king, 157.

Harsh and strong things are friendly to virtues, 74.

## B

The shepherd’s staff must be seized against the raging wolf, 173.

Christ is our bearer, 15. The poor man bears our goods, 25. He does not know how to grow weary of mercy, 170.

Balaam. What scandal he placed before the Israelite people, 27. How he blesses with a cursing mouth, 69. He was not a prophet, 159.

Baptism. Why it is given after exorcisms, 52. Those baptized before catechesis, 58. Nothing of the former offense remains from it, 60. Its soul is faith, 83. The new baptism of Magdalene, 93. It is a figure of the Lord’s three-day burial, 113. In it a person rises through newness of life. It can wash away the filth of the Jews, 137. What John’s baptism was like. What Christ’s was like. The whole Trinity is in the Jordan, and why, 157. What effects belong to Christ’s baptism. John baptized Christ, who was to receive forgiveness, 160. Christ does not serve John when John baptizes Him, but commands the sacraments. Why Christ is baptized in His own blood, 164. Its form comes from the universal flood, 166. Lent opens the baptismal font. The Lord’s baptism is one for washing souls and bodies, 171. It washes the conscience unto salvation. The eye of the baptized sinner is a drop of holy dew, 176. The form of baptism comes from Christ, and why it is such, 80. The returning son is a figure of the baptized human being, 137. The baptisms of sinners are tears, 93. The tears of the mothers of the innocent slain were baptisms, 152. Concerning its power, 34.

Blessedness. Its nature is explained learnedly, 24. David sets it before people in the Psalms so as to summon them to victory, 44. The Eucharistic bread belongs to perfect blessedness, 72. In the heavenly places, the touch of Christ is eternal, 76. Travelers and others enjoy it, 89. In blessedness itself the blessed do not cease from the duties they performed here in holiness, 121. Why those who know it through faith do not seek to possess it after death, 124. Promised to those who serve God, 161. It is truly life, 11. See Glory, Eternal, Kingdom.

Blessed is the one who keeps watch, 22. The one who anticipates the enemy’s deceits, 27. Made blessed by Christ as citizens of the holy city, 50. Blessed are those who await the Lord in hope, 71. And those whom guilt does not strike and complaint has not touched, 91. Blessed is the one who believes that he receives good things from God and accepts bad things, 123. Blessed is the one who provides for himself and others, 155. The blessed are freed from present cares, 163. The blessed see eternal things, and so forth, 176.

War must be declared against sins during Lent, 12 and 13. It has a reward corresponding to the equality of the struggle, 22. What Balaam’s wars were like, 27. Many have overcome wars who have lost the battles of the flesh, 41. The battles of the disciples’ thoughts and peace, 84. Where there is no peace of mercy, there is civil war, 104. What the wars of death are, 118. War arising from money, 126. In war, to die for the king is virtue, but greater is it to complete the struggles for him, 128. The warlike person flees by skill, not by fear, 150. He who overthrows the wars of the world desires Christ to come to him, 158. A new order of warfare, when nations go out to fight against human beings, and what follows, 171.

The trumpet of the master of wars, 14.

Benefits enlarge the devout mind toward service, not toward arrogance, 142. How can someone render service for benefits if he does not see the giver? 147.

Before one fights with beasts, the rewards are announced to him, 44. They were ordered by God to be subject to human authority, not to human art, 148. The entire ferocity of beasts is directed toward tearing apart one sheep, 171. They become more savage when they cannot seize their prey. The dancing girl was a beast, 127 and 174. Who are those who pass over into a beast? 11 and 23.

Bethlehem is called “house of bread,” and why the Lord is born there, 156.

The chariot. The Trinity ascended a two-horse chariot, 170. What He did there.

Endearments serve the vices, 74. By them a child’s mind is led toward prudence, 108. The Lord speaks tenderly to the sinful human being, 161.

The blasphemies of the Jews against Christ while He was teaching, 131.

Good works are represented in burning lamps, 22. They offend the wicked, 32. They must be concealed, 39. They possess the fruits of their labor, 97. They must be done, 158. They must be done out of obligation, 161. In them we have God as helper, 11.

Love possesses good people, 80. Life is prepared for them, 66. The mixture of good and evil does not disturb good people, but makes them [so], 47.

Goodness is the mother of virtues, 31. Through God’s goodness one is received, 81. It is hated by the wicked, 131. Goodness without equity is not found with God, nor equity without goodness, 145.

The good of the poor man in the other age will draw tears from those who here rejoiced in their own evil, 47. The Creator’s good things come first; afterward the devil’s evil things follow, 96. When and how evil is taken from good, 113. To receive good things in exchange for evils unworthily is itself evil, 123. The faithful believed that receiving good things from God meant accepting bad things. Good things harmed the rich man, 124. They were dissipated by the steward, 125. Good things are not recognized except through knowledge of evils, 131. God is the good Creator, 11.

Brevity is friendly to discourse, 132. The brevity of the human body makes it deformed, 163. The shortness of the time available for repentance should not be feared, and why, 167.

Fine linen elevated the rich man into luxury, 124. See Purple, Banqueter.

## C
- **Buried corpse:** Buried in mud, it does not know the bites of worms, 121. What it is when alive, 50.
- **To fall.** Human frailty quickly falls when it despises its companions, 170. Those who have been raised up are hurled more violently into ruin, 13.
- **Blind man:** The blind man beside the road is healed at a command, 176. Why he was born from mud. The third blind man was outside the village, and other matters. Born for darkness, not for light. Faith is given to the blind man before his eyes. Why he was asked whether he could see. He saw the dawn, not the light. After repeated treatment he saw. This blind man was a Jew.
- **Heavenly things:** How the heavenly beings are clothed, 82. The heavenly realm does not admit a sinner, 83. How earthly people become heavenly, 117. We desire to hear heavenly things only narrowly, 124. Who is not ashamed to beg in heavenly places? 125. Those desiring heavenly things cannot be ensnared by the traps of earthly things, 129. Let us direct our desire toward a heavenly dwelling. Heavenly things are understood from the Lord’s words, 139. People despise heavenly things and acquire earthly ones, 144. Whoever gives heavenly things does not lose them, and the one who receives them does not store them up for himself alone, 162. They must not be despised, 163. One who thinks about them does not lack bodily necessities. A person will have a heavenly apparel. Let us seek to grasp heavenly things, 123. In heavenly things a person is steadfast who had been wavering on earth, 57.
- **Heaven:** Those rushing from heaven seek mud, 16. What has one who possesses heaven to do with earth? 25. Why are purses necessary in it. He falls from heaven who has sinned in heavenly things, 26. The rich, looking toward heaven, trample earthly things, 54. Let heaven be the possession of earthly people, 71. A person knocks at heaven but cannot bear its burdens, 90. Heaven, made firm by the entire atmosphere, carries the waters and is not carried, 101. What is more beautiful than heaven? It is [uncertain] to speak of that which conveys us to heaven, 117. It is moved by necessity. Earth must be changed into heaven, 124. It cries out over public sin, 125. It can receive and hold the rich. It shines with the lights of the stars, 130. We were cast out of heaven through Adam and brought back to it through Christ, 159. In heaven, things clear to human eyes are darkened, 160. The penitent flies up to heaven, 167. Envy was driven from it together with the devil, 168. He was tempted by envy, 172. The one separated from earth is joined to heaven, 164. Clouds of earth darken heaven, 41. What our kingdom in heaven is like, 144.
- **Cain:** The fratricide, because of envy, 4 and 172. The consecrator of death, 96. An ungrateful high priest: what he did, 109. Carrying a twig, he found fuel by which he would be burned. Out of terror he sought death, 147. Out of the jealousy of envy he wanted to be alone, 4.
- **Caiaphas:** Why he prophesies with a profane mouth, 49.
- **Heat:** When heat is extinguished in one suffering fever, 114. Fire is nourished by cold. The rich man’s heat in hell, 122.
- **To slander:** Whoever attempts to slander the past does not deserve to see the present, 96. The true soldier does not bring slander but repels it, 137.
- **Camel:** Described, 167.
- **Canaanite woman:** By sudden faith she obtained what she was asking for, 60. About her, ibid.
- **Dog:** It betrays a stranger, disturbs a thief, and relieves the cares of servants, 60. A person is changed into a human being when he confesses himself to be a dog, and those who refuse to be sons become dogs. The rich man’s dogs fed on Lazarus’s flesh, 121 and 124. In the dogs, compassion overcame hunger, 121. By licking, they continually tend their own wounds [Col. 1149]. Dogs were set before Lazarus so that he would not have water from the rich man’s well, 122. Why a Gentile is called a dog, ibid. A rabid dog does not eat bread but human flesh, 174. A stranger bites, 40.
- **Divine songs:** They are to be taken up with other songs on the sinner’s return, 6. They are to be joined to the Lenten fast, 10. The good things arising from David’s singing; why they are called so, 14. To relieve sorrow, 46.
- **Song:** Various kinds for relieving labor, 10. It is mercenary where there is no lamentation, 19. It should resound through the instrument of holiness on the Lord’s birthday, 91. It relaxes weary spirits, 115. Mixed song is pleasant when the voice is harmonious, 116. Why farmers, sailors, and soldiers sing, 118. The Resurrection should be sung so that fear of death may cease. Singers are seductions, 127.
- **Captive:** A captive triumphing over his own tyrant inflicts great pain on him, 113. For one spiritually captive to crimes, freedom is hateful, 127. A person drags the captive demon into God’s presence, 16.
- **Head:** Christ’s head is anointed with ointment because God is in Christ’s head, 93. John’s head is devoured by the dancing girl, 127. The honor of the head extends to the members, 173. Christ is the head of the man, 174. The serpent’s head is subjected to the human being, 173. The man is in Christ the head, 80.
- **Executioner:** An executioner does nothing from himself; therefore the one who seeks his favor is wretched, 17. Envy is the executioner of its own people, 172. Worms are the executioners of the human being, 118. See **Torturer**.
- **Flesh:** How it is moved and moves others, 14. It does not delay one from meeting God if its burdens are put in order, 24. It must be restrained by the belt of self-control. The struggle against the flesh has not been overcome even by the strong, 41. It trembled when God descended into it, 68. How it is changed into spirit, 71. It will rise again for the reward of the laborer and the punishment of the sinner, 83. It is never secure concerning its own conscience, 88. Who will carry out its affairs? 89. How it presumes too much about itself, 90. Its vices sink it into mud, 94. The flesh of sin will be flesh of holiness in the resurrection, 95. The affection implanted in the flesh is changed by the devil, 96. It is changed into spirit when God wills, 102. Let it not rise up against the spirit, 110. A person devoted to the flesh is forgetful of glory, 114. Why those placed in the flesh are called exposed, 115. In the resurrection it will be possessed by the Spirit, 117. It needs little, 122. What is born from it is flesh, 142. To live in the flesh beyond the flesh is heavenly life, 143. Human flesh is advanced into the glory of God through the Incarnation, 145. Why the one who had taken mud took flesh, 148. Flesh is more precious than mud. What flesh cannot perceive is the work of the heavenly spirit, 155. Loosened through indulgence, it falls away from God, 161. Compacted through a variety of fluids, 163. It does not believe that it can be satisfied by manna alone. A person moves about in the mud of the flesh, 161. It swells through crime, 167. How, inflamed for lust, it rushes headlong, 174. It is sufficient for its own ruin and must not be constricted with wedges. What it did in Herod. Its softness of clothing is trampled under harshness, 13.
- **Cassianus, martyr:** See the note in the sermon, 165.
- **Chastity:** The distinguishing mark of Christian warfare, 22. It must be embraced, 24. It must be sacrificed to God so that lust may die, 108. John the Baptist, an example of chastity, 127. Hostile to the immodest.
- **Catechumen:** Not yet born through baptism, he calls God Father, 69, 70, and 71. He calls him Father before he sees his mother, 72. Adopted as a son in the womb so that he may be born free, 72. He reigns before he lives. In the womb he acknowledges himself to be of heavenly stock. He is to be brought to baptism by Nero, 10. See **Church**, the sermon on the Creed, and the Lord’s Prayer.
- **Chains:** What the chains of the rich man’s barns did, 104.
- **Chair:** How the philosopher, Pharisee, and heretic establish the chair of pestilence, 44. The stone of Christ’s tomb was the chair of heavenly doctrine, 75.
- **Cause:** Whoever wishes to take responsibility for another makes the other’s case his own, 151. The causes of things, so that they may be investigated, 101. One easily strays from justice who fears human beings rather than God in legal cases, 127.
- **Storerooms:** Worthless things must be despised so that we may eat everything; how, 163.
- **Number one hundred:** What it signifies, 168. The hundredfold fruit is owed to God, 126. Whoever desires to reach the hundredfold fruit should imitate the centurion, 25. This is desired by hearers of the divine word, 136.
- **Centurion:** Concerning him, see 15 and 102 throughout.
- **Contest:** The greatness of the reward is proposed according to the greatness of the contest, 22. Crowns are announced beforehand to one about to undertake the most serious contests, 44. What one who wishes to compete should abstain from, 119. Here one must compete for the heavenly crown, 144. See **Contest**, **War**, **Wrestling**, **Soldier**, **Reward**.
- **Chaldaeans:** Investigators of the stars, 156. Astrologers do not worship the one God without a god; they serve as many gods in heaven as there are stars, ibid. See **Magi**, **Astrology**.
- **Charity:** It joins us to God, 4. Whoever does not have charity is without God, 53. Let it be preserved, 6. It has no deceit, 55. God’s charity toward the human being, 69 throughout. We are carried by charity, 81. Through it the debt owed to God is repaid, 94. It helps with the past; it is the guardian of holiness, 14. A human being returns nothing comparable to divine charity, 110. Whoever does not believe in Christ does not have Christ’s charity, 119. It is God’s gift, 135. It should be mingled with freedom in correcting the brethren, 139. What it did toward God, 147. It is signified by gold, 159. If charity exists, it does not perish, 162. It is the greater and better inheritance, 3. It grows through death, 164. It is violated by envy, 172. It is tested by gifts, 10.
- **Bond of indebtedness:** Necessary until the debt is restored, 62. What Adam’s paternal debt was before Christ, 123. Christ opened and erased it. At least half of the bonds for debts owed to the master are to be discharged, 125. They must be moderated with devout assent, 126. Why the steward is praised for cancelling his master’s bonds, 126. The bond of oil reached the Gentiles. What the chorus is: read 4. See **Harmony**.
- **Chrism:** See **Oil**, **Ointment**.
- **Christian:** The principle of Christian warfare is fasting, 8. The Christian’s humble return is shown in the figure of the prodigal son, 1. What sons of rams he leads to Christ, 10. He must not fear demons, 17. Their tranquility, 20. He is called glorious, 22. They are called new wineskins, 31. They share in glory under the yoke of devotion, 35. Their childhood is animated by lighter commandments, 38. He must surpass vices with virtues, 5. Why their beginnings are formed through injuries, 38. Armed with prayer, fasting, and mercy, he does not fear, 43. He should learn from the example of the Hebrews, 46. He is brought to his homeland by sailing, 50. He must not linger on the roads of Jewish faithlessness. Let him send his possessions to heaven, 54. **Christian doctrine:** see **Doctrine**. The Christian should sanctify Christ’s name by his conduct, 69. When a Gentile dishonors the Christian name. He is designated, not raised into divine offspring, 71. He should await God’s inheritance. He knows that creatures are assigned to his service, 89. He eats of Christ, 95. He calls people to Christ and leads them to him, 102. He loves the Hebrew people while confessing that Christ came from them. By word alone, not by bodily presence, he perceived the Lord’s powers. Christians are cruel toward the poor and captives, 103. Christians are made through the laying on of hands, 105. Ordained by Paul as high priest and victim, 108. How he should walk in newness of life, 113. How he should bear the image of his creator, 117. How he should rise again. To avoid fearing death, he should meditate on the Resurrection, 118. He receives the crown of glory, 119. He must not be polluted by pagan spectacles, 155. He should draw the erring away from sins, 155. He renounces the devil, 158. He should return to heaven by another way, 159. Certain of life, kingdom, and immortality, he should not be anxious about clothing, 163 and throughout the sermons. The simple believer and the learned believer differ concerning faith, 166. Christians who follow the world and do not wish judgment to come are harder than the Jews, 167. Let him follow the lamp of Mother Church, 169. The repentance of the Christian people shone forth in one sinner who repented. Believing himself to be a son of God, let him answer his lineage, 10. From what we are called Christians, 60. He dies to the Law so that he may live by grace, 115. The belt of chastity is the distinguishing mark of Christian warfare, 22. How the members of Christians ought to work, 120. How the birth of the primitive Church of the Christians was consecrated, 175.
- **Chrysologus:** In his time there was a great storm in the Church of God, and what it was, 20 and 21. While preaching, his voice failed him, 35. At the end of the sermon he used brevity, 36. At dawn he stood before the Lord with the brethren, 39. He asked God for knowledge of the Scriptures. How he excuses himself with Saint Adelphus the bishop, 39 and 136. What he did for the salvation of unbelievers, 40. In his time there was pestilence and famine, 45. In his time the nations were fishing throughout the whole world for Christ, 47. His hearers restrained themselves, 51. He taught the Creed to little children in the faith, 56. He led the old to the faith, 61. He baptized Gentiles even before the catechism had been completed, 58. He called the nations to faith, 59. He told the hearers of the Creed to be silent, 59. He forbade the mysteries of faith to be given to books but commanded them to be entrusted to memory; this is found in the sermon on the Creed, 56–62. In teaching little children he reduced himself wholly to a child, 62. He taught catechumens the Lord’s Prayer, 71. Through the labor of vigils and the weariness of fasting he fell silent from preaching, 74. Returning from a journey among his people, he resumed his sermons, 75. He was tired from the journey. Out of compassion he was unable to explain the Lord’s Passion, 77. With God revealing the Scriptures, he expounds them, 82. The reasons why he was silent in preaching, 86. The people wept at his announced silence. He commonly calls his hearers “brothers,” 88 and elsewhere. He desires to be the Lord’s ointment, 93. With God as author, he explains the sacraments of the Gospel, 94. With the Holy Spirit revealing them, 95, 97, and 109. He does not expound Scripture because of his hearers’ weariness, 101. He is grieved that money is not given at the altar for the redemption of captives and for the poor, 103. His sermon lasted for an hour and more, 112. Christ was in him, 116. Whom he calls a concise preacher, 120. He postponed to another hearing what he could not explain in one sermon, 122. He expounded the Gospel soberly, 125. He prayed to God to pour knowledge into the minds of his hearers, 126. His inward parts were shaken by Herod’s impiety, 127. He preaches when he is consecrated archbishop at Ravenna, 130. In that sermon he discusses the office of a bishop. He praises the empress and asks the priests to pray for the rulers at the end. He calls his hearers holy brothers, 141. He calls his hearers his life, salvation, and glory, 147. He reproves pagan corruption, 155. He preaches before the sacred service, 160. In a brief sermon he embraces extensive matters. He preaches in Latin; this is gathered from 159. He consecrates Saint Projectus to the bishopric of Forum Cornelii, 165 throughout. He was initiated into sacred office by Saint Cornelius. He consecrates Marcellinus bishop of Vicohaventia, 175 throughout. He reproves varied and immoderate fasting, 166. He preaches before the first day of Lent. What he advises his sheep concerning his preaching, 173. He preaches from a step and from the priestly seat. He recognized that he was capable of understanding the Scriptures only through God, 5. He urges catechumens to receive baptism quickly, 5 and sermon 59. See **Peter the bishop**.
- **Food:** What diseases the indigestion of foods produces, and the restriction of those foods, 41. Foods are prepared to relax minds after labor, 93. How food should be taken by those dining together, 127. The Lord eats many kinds of food, but the servant eats a half-cooked little dinner, 161. A person does not believe that one kind of food is sufficient for him, 163. Health-giving food is bitter to those with fever, 164. The soul’s food must be moderated, 166. Our food is led by the devil into gluttony, 12. Lust is restrained by rustic food, 13. Food given to the dead, 17.
- **Haircloth:** Made from goat hair, 167. It removes bodily uncleanness.
- **Belt:** A sign of servitude, 24. It must be taken up as a sign of chastity. The flesh must be restrained by it.
- **Ashes:** They enrich the earth, 164.
- **To look around:** What it means to look around toward Christ, 32.
- **City; citizen:** The splendor of a city invites its ruler to dwell there, 171. A citizen ought to draw a fellow citizen away from sin, 155. A citizen pays a tax; a soldier receives pay, 166. The envy of citizens, 48. A city of faithlessness described, 95.
- **Cry:** A cry must be raised to the Lord when we see dangers threatening ourselves or our brothers, 20. The cry ceases where there is no hearer, 167.
- **Key:** As the royal key opens the first door, so it makes the other inner chambers accessible, 44. Why the Pharisee had received the keys of knowledge, 172.
- **Banquet:** The rich man’s banquet described, 161. The apostles prepared the Lord’s banquet for the Church upon its tables. How Peter’s banquet was arranged, 163. Herodian. See **Herod**.
- **Thought:** The sins of thought are not avoided, 30. Human thoughts do not penetrate God’s mysteries without God, 81. No one can think outside himself, 104. The vain thought of the human being. The rich man’s thought was scattered. Judgment is mature before the answer, 140. What a person ought to think about, so that he may attribute what is useful to God and what is useless to himself, 161. God lays human thoughts bare, 163. Through thought a person does not reach what he reaches through faith. Evil thoughts proceed from one person against another, 171. How they are conquered by the name of the Lord and the sign of the cross. The confused family of thoughts moves about in the dwelling of conscience, 15.
- **Knowledge:** Knowledge of evils provides knowledge of good things, 131.
- **Dove:** The wings of the dove should be taken up to avoid aerial powers, 98. Noah’s dove announces that the Flood has departed, and the dove of the Holy Spirit that the world’s shipwreck has ceased, 160. Against the dove are countless filthy birds, 171.
- **Pillar:** The pillar of fire drives away the darkness of ignorance, 170. The pillar of cloud moderates the heats of the mind.
- **Fellowship:** Fellowship with a brother in the present will also exist in the future, 4. Fellowship must be urged in common speech, 43. The sacrilegious person despises fellowship with God, 30. See **Union**.
- **Compassion:** None toward one’s neighbors, 20. It causes grief. What the compassion of Christ suffering caused in our author, 77. Christ’s compassion toward the returning prodigal, 3.
- **Compensation:** If possible and customary offerings are not made in place of the greatest things, there is no excuse, 114.
- **Things permitted:** Whoever seeks what is not permitted loses what is permitted, 152.
- **Preacher:** He ceases preaching because of excessive heat, following the author’s example, 51. He should be heard kindly, 76. Without Christ he has nothing to give back to his hearers, 77. Because of the weariness of his hearers, he does not expound Scripture as he ought, 101. He should preach for fruitfulness, 136. He is silent about what should be said lest the stubborn become contemptuous, 137. He should say what he is going to do and do it, and he himself should not offend. He should command the hearers to pray that they may receive the word of God, 144. He is silent, overcome by the greatness of the mystery, 146. By speaking briefly he relieves labor, 96. He should ask God for grace in speaking and the hearers for the desire to hear. How he is both fisherman and fowler, 107. He sometimes yields to haste and time, 112. The hearer is more willing when he explains doctrine in various ways, 116. He should ascend to heaven before teaching others to ascend, 120. How he may be heard with benefit, 136. He excuses himself, 138. He should preach extemporaneously, 139. He should do what he teaches, 167. He himself should be in the dress of a penitent. What he advises the people concerning listening to preaching, 173. He should not explain God’s deeds too lavishly, 95. How he should strike hearers in preaching by Christ’s example, 164. See **Sermon**, **Teacher**, **Master**.
- **Harmony:** It exists when, under the order of one Lord, a diverse household is one in will, 68. The harmony of those praying obtains everything, 132. See **Union**. Why harmony is depicted on the tablets of kings or brothers, 149. The demon seeks to tear it apart. What harmony of heaven and earth, joined together, means, 148.
- **Desire:** The beauty of form leads to it, 116. To serve desires is to live in sin, 113. See **Frailty**. Those born from desire: see **Born**.
- **Condemnation:** From Christ’s coming, the sentence of human condemnation ceased, 90. While it remains, the condemned person is not justified, 110. Through Christ the condemnation of death was dissolved. Eternal condemnation is the wrath of God, 137.
- **Confession of faith and sins:** Through the door of faith it introduces us, 6. When despised, it deserves death, 29. Why and how confession must be made, 29 and 30; it is prevented by shame and embarrassment, 34. Confession of sins should be made at Christ’s feet, 94. How sin may be forgiven without confession, 34. How confession precedes God, 46. From the watchtower of confession, the giver of forgiveness is seen, 54. It is the entrance to salvific life, 56. It is made with the mouth. Let it be inflamed, 57. What gives salvation and from where it comes, 60. Confession of faith is made with the mouth for salvation, 61. What it is useful for, 71. Through the fragrance of the fields, the fruits of confessions, 73. At the end of life one must turn to the advocacy of confession, 125. Confession is signified by myrrh, 159. See **Sinner**.
- **Confessor:** The holy confessor dies daily for the Lord when he conquers his enemies, 128. In him virtue is more perfect than in a martyr. He desires Christ to come to his palm, 158. See **Saints**, **Just**.
- **Conflict:** The conflict between the rich and the poor on earth is watched in heaven, 124.
- **Confusion:** It clings to vices, 31. The confusion of the good and the evil in this age does not disturb the good, 47. The mixture of good and evil will be weighed by separation. The confusion of the future judgment is to be feared, 125.
- **Crimes:** See **Crime**.
- **Assembly, or gathering:** Both the gathering and councils of the saints obtain everything, 132. Through negligence in prayer, the assembly of the saints disperses the body of Christ. From the unity of the members comes salvation; from separation, destruction. In a good gathering, in a bad separation. See **Harmony**, **Union**, **Charity**.
- **Married couples:** Let there be one spirit and one virtue in them, 91. They are joined by God, and how, 99. Death is the devil’s spouse, 158.
- **Marriage:** It is unique when one mind exists in two people, 89. It is not required of one who wishes to compete here, 119. Why it was permitted to priests under the old Law, 92. Through the marriage of sinners, the whole structure of the world was dissolved, 120. See **Matrimony**.
- **Conscience:** It expelled the human being from God’s sight, 6. An evil conscience drives one to ruin, 75. The flesh is not secure concerning its conscience, 88. From the tree of knowledge it is cold; from the mustard tree it becomes hot, 99. Temporal allurements are adapted to human consciences, 114. The heat of the banqueter’s conscience in torments, 122. In hell he gasps in the flame of his crime. Through the Gospel Christ opens the conscience, 125. At judgment the guilty person will blush more from conscience than from the fire of Gehenna. When it was confronted by the steward, 126. From a good conscience there is no punishment among the condemned, 135. A deceitful conscience dares nothing openly, 158. It is washed away by Christ’s baptism, 171. Fear and trembling of conscience, 36.
- **Consent:** Consent is always equal to deeds, and how, 155.
- **Counsel:** The devil is betrayed by his counsels, 13. Balaam’s scandalous counsel, 27. What the counsel of impiety did, 44. See **Impious**. Once the counsel of impiety has been accepted, nothing of piety remains, 104. Who should take counsel with himself? When human counsel is lacking, divine help soon comes, 175.
- **Comforter:** He is not lacking to the one threatened by a persecutor, 86. The devil is a bad comforter, 13.
- **Custom:** It fails when miracles are performed, 153.
- **End of the age:** How it will come about, 47.
- **Contagion:** When a Gentile avoids the contagion of the world, 23. It is called carnal sin, 59. Through the contagion of wolves, rabid sheep tore apart the shepherd Christ, 100.
- **Contempt of God:** It makes our times evil, 43. Contempt leads to patience, 124. Those who despise the Law become stubborn, 137.
- **Contention:** The mother of dissensions, 110. Furious contention had driven life far from us. Let there be no contention in the inheritance; let avarice be removed, 162.
- **Contentment:** Each person ought to be content with the gift given to him by God, 120.
- **Contrition:** How it is to be cultivated, 125. A person should turn to it when summoned to account. How it is acquired gradually, 167.
- **Controversy:** Among whom it is carried on, 122.
- **Stubborn:** The sinner becomes stubborn and rebellious when he transgresses against the Law, 116. From one who despises comes one who is stubborn, 137. It is piety not to instruct a stubborn person about the Law.
- **Conversion:** The conversion of the sinner in Matthew the tax collector: read 28 and 30. A human being sins, and God turns toward him, 45. Conversion of the senses drives away adversity, 46. Let conversion take place today. Sudden conversion to faith, 60 and 61. The conversion of a sinner is sometimes owed to a holy teacher, 107. Christ asked for the sinner’s conversion, 108. Christ promises forgiveness for conversion from sins, 125. The Lord delays judgment so that the sinner may be converted, 167. See **Repentance**, **Fear**.
- **Convicted:** The one convicted before God, summoned as accused, is called to receive forgiveness, 125.
- **Feast:** Why Jesus went to the feasts of sinners, 29 and 30. Feasts are harmful to the soul, 41. The secret of the feast does not presume to enter when uninvited, 93. The feast of Mary Magdalene’s repentance is wondrous. Whoever feasts with Christ lives forever, 95. At Christ’s feast everything contained in creation is given. How a feast should be conducted, 127. The birthdays of the saints are not celebrated in extravagant feasts, 129. The rich man’s feast is described, 161. Through a feast we seek to overcome the burden of work and labor, 170. Everything was polluted at the Pharisees’ feast, 171. What evils long feasts give birth to, 174. In Peter’s house Christ was not seeking a feast, 18. Herod’s feast. See **Herod**, **Food**, **Drunkenness**, **Eucharist**.
- **Kitchen:** One who searches out the filth of kitchens while possessing royal apparel is wholly servile in spirit, 163.
- **Heart:** The heart is brought down to vices by an overloaded belly, 2. We enter into God through the heart, 6. The heart is penetrated by God alone, 50. Between the heart and the tongue lies the matter of salvation, 56. It is satisfied with heavenly fire, 57. The heart is the ark and library of faith, 58. The stony heart of faithlessness must be removed, 65. The heart is heaven, in which Christ reigns, 75. Not to sin in the heart is the greatest thing, 89. It belongs to God to disclose the heart’s secret, 94. We speak to God with the heart, 97. We are joined to God by the heart, not by the body, 102. How hearts are dissolved by disturbances, 116. So that furrowed and sown hearts may produce growth, 119. How God tried to open the rich man’s heart, 121. The sinner feigns a heart in order to extort repentance from himself, 125. Hearts must be illuminated by God, 126. The hearts of little children are broken by tears, 128. God judges hearts, not words, 142. Human hearts endure countless crimes, 171. By what water hearts are cleansed. How the sins of the heart are conquered. God is invited to dwell in a cleansed heart. God measures deeds from hearts, 9. What dwells in the heart, 15. The hall of the heart is not without the noise of vices. The absence of the body does not harm hearts joined by faith, 32. See **Spirit**, **Mind**, **Sense**.
- **Cornelius the centurion:** He had the Holy Spirit before baptism, 60.
- **Cornelian Church:** Specially loved by Chrysologus, 165.
- **Cornelius, bishop of Forum Cornelii:** Chrysologus’s spiritual father. See the note concerning him.
- **Crown:** Crowns are announced beforehand to one about to undertake the most serious contests, 44. Crowns are owed to hermits and to those who compete in the world, 107. The Apostle urges people toward the crown of glory, 119. Many run, but the Catholic receives the crown. How one must run for the crown, at the end. We receive as many crowns as the vices we overcome. A crown is reserved for the victor, 128. Heavenly crowns are given to those serving as soldiers on earth, 144. See **Soldier**, **Triumph**.
- **Body:** Our body is a mystical ship, 8. It is mortified when the soul departs from it. What the demon reduces it to through gluttony and drunkenness, 12. What it is: it is the bed of our pain, 14. Dead without the soul, 19. Human bodies receive new wine, 31. Bodily presence is of no benefit when the mind is absent, 32. Let no one grieve over the shortness of the body, 54. It must be washed so that we may draw near to the Lord, 59. The dissolution of the body advances it toward something better, 101. Why the killers of bodies are not to be feared. The body is a servant, though precious, 102. It becomes sick unto death. It is with you; see **With you**. When the body is offered to God without the body, 108. It is a victim if it is without sin. When does it live? The body is governed on earth by the soul, 109. Sins seize the body, and other matters. Let the body accompany the soul to heaven. The body of one suffering fever is described, 111. Bodily permissions are to be despised by the lustful, 113. The body of sin: see **Sin**. By what things the body is more greatly tormented in fever, 114. Christ’s body freed us from crime, 115. The body and anguish of the mind, 116. Crimes pour forth from a corrupted body, 120. The mystical body reformed by God, as it ought to be. For what purpose our body is adorned with virtues. Why the poor man’s body is full of wounds, 121. Money rules bodies, 126. What the divided joining and joined division of bodies teaches us, 132. How God and the human being are mingled in one body, 142. The reins must not be loosened for the body, 161. The body consists of various members, 163. A body is beautiful if it is tall; what is attained by faith, not by thought, 163. Nothing is greater than its increase. A person moves about in the mud of the body, 161. Cures of bodies are performed by God; why and how, 176. See **Members**, **Christ the human being**.
- **Correction:** When secret correction is of no benefit, public confusion follows, 127. Correction of a criminal gives birth to hatred. John corrects by analogy, 137. Fraternal correction consists in reproving as a judge and forgiving as a brother, 139. Let charity be mingled with freedom in it. How it is to be carried out. Whoever thinks of nothing concerning correction hopes for nothing concerning forgiveness, 158. One corrected by God is soon comforted, 163. How a servant of God is corrected by God himself when he thunders against the Pharisees, 171.
- **Corruption:** It perishes in the resurrection, not the flesh, 117. What corruption, the sister of death, advises the human being, 118. It is always the stepmother of things, 146. The corruption of human frailty arises from the foulness of vices, 167. Corrupted body: see **Body**.
- **Raven:** The bird is described, 163.
- **Gluttony and drunkenness:** What evils they cause, 1. Our food is led by the demon into gluttony, 12. The devil rules gluttony, 13. How it conquered the strong, 41. The miser belches the indigestion of gluttony toward heaven, 121. A mind weighed down by gluttony judges badly, 173. See **Drunkenness**, **Food**.
- **Created things:** All created things are very good because they were created by God, 89. Good from the beginning, they were made evil by the devil, 96. Made by command alone, they must again be dissolved by command alone, 101. It is grievous that created things perish. What is more beautiful than created things? Their description, 103. In themselves they are not evil, but through them an occasion for sinning is given, 116. Created things were worshiped by the human being as though they were God. Creation from nothing, 48. Creation and re-creation arise from one and the same power, 80. Creation and our re-creation are from the whole Trinity, 157.
- **Creator:** He is known through contemplation of creation, 89. Christ, creator of all things, is salvation to the faithful and ruin to the unfaithful. He is not constrained by the laws of nature, 90. In the beginning he made all things very good, 96. For the Creator, creation does not perish; rather, antiquity perishes with time, 101. Let us be devoted to the Creator so that creation may be devoted to us, 103. The Creator is not comprehended by human reasoning, 131.
- **Creation:** It does not know whether it should marvel more that God is human or that the human being is God, 72. At the time of Christ’s Passion, all creation suffers with him, 77. It flees injury to the Creator, and how, 78. It does not resist the Creator but serves him, 84. It stands between vices and virtues, 89. It was subjected to the devil’s art and tested, 96. Human creation is joined to God in one body, 140. In its entirety it does not contain God, 140 and 142. At Christ’s birth creation was not destroyed, 144. The terror of creation, which could not see God, 147. The evils arising from this. All creation comes together for the Creator’s meal, 163. All creatures tremble at the sight of God, 6. See **Creator**.
- **To believe:** One believes with the heart for righteousness, 56. The person who believes that God is the creator possesses everything, 56. Divine mysteries are to be believed, 59. How we believe in God. Where faith comes from, 60. What must be believed is to be entrusted to the heart, not to paper, 61. What we believe with the heart, let us confess with the mouth. Why the forgiveness of sins and the resurrection of the flesh must be believed, 61. The question “how?” is not appropriate for one who believes, 62. By believing we grant ourselves forgiveness; by despairing we fall into sins. Those who wish what they have heard not to be believed do not wish what they have seen to be reported, 66. Let the believer, confessing himself a son of God, answer his lineage, 68. What believing is worth is shown, 71. It is madness for a person not to believe what he desires to happen to himself, 74. Whoever believes more deeply doubts more profoundly. Nor is the one deceived who believes what is difficult, 79. To believe quickly is to fall quickly. The world believed in Christ without seeing him, 83. It is caution to believe humbly about God and slowly, 90. Zacharias possessed within himself a rule of believing, 90. In peace many believe in Christ, but in persecution there are few martyrs, 97. Jesus reveals himself obscurely as God for the sake of our faith, 102. Earlier generations believe future things, later generations believe past things, and how, 110. One believes without reason if he believes he was born in order to perish, 118. The Resurrection is shown as something to be believed through examples. See **Resurrection**. Christ must be believed faithfully, 119. One returning from the underworld does not deserve to be believed if he did not believe Christ, 123. Faith perceives God, 131. The Magi are the leaders of the faith of the Gentiles, 159. What a Christian ought to believe, and how, at length, 83. The Jews did not wish to believe Christ, 123. They even try to prevent others from believing in him, 131. The almsgiver believes in eternal life in another age, 54.
- **Creditor:** When he is a debtor, and conversely, 88. The heavenly creditor repays the whole debt through charity, 96. The heavenly creditor is present everywhere and always, 126. Nor is he forestalled by fraud.
- **Debt:** The greater the credit, the greater the debt, 26. To postpone is characteristic of a shameless debtor; to pay at once, of an honorable one, 123. What it means to squander God’s credit, 125. The one who preserves the credit of innocence does not pay interest in punishment, 167. Divine credit does not require human security, 62.
- **Crime:** The father bears the crimes of the son, though he does not bear his nakedness, 3. Lovers of crimes accuse virtues, 32. Crime corrupts the conscience, 62. Blessed are those whom crime does not touch, 91. The support of crimes comes from the bad interpretation of the divine word, 113. To succumb to crimes is to live in sin. Freed from every crime through Christ’s body, 115. Crimes increase while they are being cut down, 116. Through sin, crime rules. The origin of crimes is madness, 117. What the confusion of crimes does harmfully, 120. In the resurrection, crime perishes, not the person, 117. The greatness of crimes destroys the greatness of virtues, 127. Birds of crimes must be driven away by the spear of the cross, 171. Who are Herod’s witnesses to crime? 174. What is a matter of crime must not be considered a matter of nature, 11. The magnitude of a crime is established from place, person, and office, 54. When is torment not small? 132. See **Affliction**.
- **Cruelty:** It rages when it sees itself spreading, 152. It is always possessed by madness, 173. Why the cruel person adds himself to Mars, 155. Mercy must not be extended to the cruel, 127. One who is cruel toward the poor becomes more savage toward himself, 123.
- **Cross:** It must be carried after God, not before him, 54. It is the life-giving wood. Through the cross, greater things were restored to us than we had lost through the tree of paradise, 60. It was received ardently by Andrew and Peter, 133. The devil wished to take it away from us, 150. Birds of crimes must be driven away by the spear of the cross, 171. The sails of the mind must be spread on the tree of the cross, 8.
- **Fault:** Fault and vengeance were taking everything away, 42. What happened to nature because of fault, 87. Through fault we lose confidence in the face, 93. The fault of one flowed down into punishment for all, 111. In the resurrection, fault perishes, not the human being, 117. Fault was condemned at Christ’s birth, 144.
- **Divine worship:** It must be rendered with understanding, 109.
- **Maternal womb:** The maternal cradle receives the crying human being, 133.
- **Wedges:** They are troops of vices, 43. They are not necessary for constricting the flesh, 174. Wedges of enemies, 152.
- **Desire:** What it does when it rushes headlong toward wealth, 1. It is acquired from profit and from possession, 7. It is death or night, 8. He fasts for it who does not fast for the poor.

D

Christ satisfies the greed of the greedy—how, 25. Greed oppresses, 29 and 30. It makes the hand withered, 32. Who, unharmed by the smoke, can pass through the fires of greed? 89. Greed for riches, 104, passim. Human greed deceives the mind, 117. How human begging comes about, so that inhuman greed may be exposed, 121. What precipitous and heedless greed does, 162. See Avarice, Riches.

Care for earthly things must be despised, 163. No care is difficult when life is dear, 167. The healing of the bent woman—which, 105, and following. An enemy of care is one who neither desires treatment nor to be healed, 113. If one who has been healed does not remain under treatment, he sins; likewise, if he abandons fire, iron, or medicines, 114. He does not treat who awaits the sick person’s decision. Sin makes the treatment weaker [*languiorem*, uncertain reading], 116. Those curious about the stars and the world, but negligent of their own salvation, are rebuked by the Lord, 164. Excessive curiosity is condemned and harmful. See Astrologer.

Whoever knows how to run better receives the crown, 119. Let Jews, philosophers, heretics, and Christians run here for the crown of glory. How we ought to run with faithful perseverance for the crown. The martyr Cyprian, triumphing over the devil, left us an example of the virtues, 129. On the day of his death a crowd of evil people stood by; at the festival, a multitude of the faithful rejoices.

D
### Condemned

The condemned are unfit for heavenly things at the last judgment, 122. Why the condemned is called a son by Abraham, 123. They have nothing to do with mercy, 124. They are under God’s wrath, 137. They are more tormented by the happiness of the blessed than by Gehenna, 66. See *Hell*.

Daniel saw God the Father judging, and Christ—how, 131.

### Food

Various dishes, according to human opinion, ought to nourish the body, 163. See *Feasts*.

### Give

We ought to give God what he wants, so that we may receive from him what we want, 41. Whoever does not give should not complain if he does not receive, 103. Give God what you can, and you will be accepted, 110. We ought to give our own possessions as alms and promptly return what belongs to others, 123.

### David

The prophet David acts as a physician for sinners in the first psalm, 44. He prays for the coming Messiah, 45. And for himself, although he is holy. The psalms are called David’s harp, 115. Prophetic melody, 116. David, while Saul was pursuing him, receives hospitality from the surrounding region [reading uncertain], 150. David’s harp is to be played at the sinner’s return, 6. What David did with the pipe and song, 10. The father of Joseph in the twenty-eighth generation, 145.

### Demoniac

How the demoniac is healed by Christ, 51. Why he ought to be brought to Christ. The demon suffered in him. Why Christ asks in him for the time of suffering. How he suffers, 17. See *Possessed*.

### Demon

See *Devil*.

### Debts

Debts owed to God must be paid, or one must pray that they be forgiven, even when they are not understood, 123. Debts forgiven by Christ in his passion. Christ paid the earlier debts on our behalf, 125. Debts are not to be increased by adding unlawful obligations when one can scarcely pay what is owed, 137. To ask for more than is owed is to demand fraud, not tribute. A debtor who does not fulfill agreements is crafty, 5. He uses shame when his loans are publicly defamed, 9. The honorable man promptly fulfills his promises, 36. To be always in debt is distressing, 88. Where the creditor is the debtor, and conversely, there is a contract of love. [Col. 1156] Delay granted to debtors increases the creditor’s favor, 89. His promise must be awaited. Debt is repaid by love, 94. How much a human being owes God. It belongs to a shameless debtor either to delay what has been entrusted to him or to deny what he has promised, 123. It belongs to the honorable man to pay both promptly. A human being should acknowledge himself a debtor to God. If a debtor’s sense of shame is removed, innocence is violated, 126. It is human that a debtor seeks fraudulent advantages. God is our debtor and the executor of our debt—how, 25. To pay one’s debts is profitable, 126.

### Decalogue

What evils result if its commandments are not observed, 169. Christ was hidden within it. The defender of the law becomes its enemy—how, 96. A defender ought to be a soldier, not an extortioner, 137. See *Soldier*.

### Disfigurement

The disfigurement of the invited person is an insult to the one who invited him, 23. The disfigurement of a human being arising from bodily shortness, 163.

### Deicides

The Jews were deicides—how, 172, with note.

### Offenses

Whoever scrutinizes offenses exposes them, 3. The power of love does not see them, 21. They are compensated by grief, 30. In offenses a person is regarded as acting voluntarily, 35. At the judgment concerning offenses, the merciful will not be judged, 42. Sweet things entice toward offenses, 74. Whoever walks in offenses has the devil on his head, 105. Our offenses are erased by Christ’s death, 110. Offenses must be anticipated so that they may be trampled down, 116. How they deceive us. They could not previously be overcome until sin was extinguished through Christ. Offenses have deadly blandishments, 117. Offenses will end in the resurrection of the flesh, 117. Through the diseases of offenses the image of the Creator has been removed, 120. Offenses forgiven by Christ in his suffering, 123. They must be forgiven one’s neighbor, 139. It is useful to secure forgiveness for oneself before offenses occur, 2. How they are to be driven from our hearts, 171. See *Sin*, *Vice*, *Crime*, *Debt*.

### Descend

Zacchaeus is commanded to descend so that he may ascend, 54.

### Deserts

The deserts to which John preached were deserts of disciplines, not of human beings or places, 167.

### Desire

The desire of Christians must be directed toward a heavenly dwelling, 129. It is evil to be enslaved to one’s own desires, 132. Desire is the child of love, 147. See *Love*.

### Despair

Whoever despairs slips into every sin, 62. God can restore to the despairing what he promises, 90. Christ went to care for them, 16. God gives salvation to the despairing, 65. Despair, the worst of all evils, always comes as the final stage in adversity, 83. It was reproached in the apostles. Let it be far from the sinner, 94. What does the servant of death persuade a person to do? 118. It casts a person down, 71.

### Destruction

The devil always begins with it, 104. How the destruction of the body of sin takes place, 113.

### Devotion

Cautious devotion is rewarded; presumptuous servitude is punished, 109. It should be more cautious before God than before human beings. Perfect devotion owes to an image what it owes to a king, 147. A devoted spirit grows through the insignia of benefits toward service, not toward pride, 142.

### God

God is called human, 5. His name and mercy, 6. The life of the soul, 19. Executor and debtor, 25. Compared with the sun and a physician, 35. He can do everything by command, 34. He is always wholly present everywhere, 34. With him death is sleep. God, who is everywhere, has nowhere to flee from himself, 37. The great Lord, even in our body, 46. He perfects all things from nothing. He heals by command, 49. He torments demons, 52. His providence, 18. How he is said to possess anger, 45. He does not need what belongs to us, 22. How he ministers glory to the blessed, 24. At the sight of him all things tremble, 6. After fasting he does not seek bread, 12. He is Lord of health, 15. How he is said to make use of passions, 32. He is not polluted by senses or human thoughts, 35. The wounds of sins, not of bodies, offend God’s sight, 35. He hears those who are silent and sees what is hidden. He is not diminished in a human being. He cannot be defiled by touching his creature, 36. Where God is, there is no sin, 44. He neither eats nor hungers, 11. God’s goodness, 23. He sees the human heart, 50. Creator of what is good, 11. He gives the ability to do what he commands and does what he orders. He created the human being with his hand and everything else by his word, 33. He gives and takes away temporal things, 46. God is one, but not solitary, 57.

God the Father has a Son—and how. He has many sons by grace, but only one by nature. The Son of God is coeternal with the Father, 58. The Son is a seed remaining eternally within the eternal Begetter, 59. Nothing can be added to God, 58. God is one, but in Trinity, 60. How God the Father begets the Son, 60. Almighty, 60 and 62. He is almighty; in himself, from himself, and always has the Son with himself, 61. God neither defrauds nor is defrauded, 62. He retains what has been stolen and possesses what has been denied. God’s own order is always secure. The Son of God always existed, 62. God the Father begets the Son while revealing him to us, 62. Places do not make God absent, nor do times represent him, 63. He gives from himself and does not ask from himself. What stinks to a human being does not stink to God, 65. Author of the ages. Everything between the Father and the Son is carried out in love. God’s promise is certain, 68. Though inaccessible to the mind, he communicated himself to the human being, 69. God made human suffers adversity. He dies. He taught how to pray. That God should be bread. [Col. 1157] 71.

God made human is the dread of the saints, 72. God is the kingdom and contains in himself the whole power of the kingdom, 72. He is not diminished in the flesh, 76. He is not seen in a place of faithlessness, 80. The Son of God conferred upon humanity what he had always possessed with the Father and the Spirit. He restores to salvation the one whom he created for life. God is the name of the Trinity, 83. God is almighty because he can forgive every sin. God is the one who lives from death and rises from a wound, 84. He does not learn letters but teaches, 85. He gives speech and silence, 86. Who God is, without whom there is no other—how, 88. Everything created by God is good, 89. The desired one, unknown and unseen even by angels, is known through John, 90. He closes and opens human mouths; he makes the barren fruitful, and conversely. He can do what he wills and restore to the despairing what he promises. For God, to will is to do; to give is to promise. With God there is no guilt where there is no fault, 92. When he stands, he rebukes; when he sits, he judges; with those prostrate he lies beside them when he reclines, 93.

God is at the head of Christ and in the feet of those evangelizing peace. He made all good things from the beginning; what he made for the human being, 96. What God himself guards does not perish for him, 97. Witness of fraud and labor. God’s weakness is stronger than human beings, his foolishness wiser, and his least thing more magnificent than the whole greatness of the world, 98. He can do what he wills, 100. Author of life, not of death, 101. So that his deep mysteries may be known, 101. Why he did not destroy death together with its author from the beginning. His command establishes the waters above heaven, and so forth; he manifested himself obscurely in the flesh in order to leave room for faith, 102. By the Word he made all things and remade them: from nothing he created, from something he restores. God is the way, the truth, and the life, 108. He is not the author of death, 112. God is not forestalled by fraud, 126. He is not seen by bodily eyes, 131. Nor is it a matter of how great he is, but that he is. His substance and image differ from those of an angel. God the Father speaks to the Son when he says, “Let us make the human being in our image.” Before granting divine benefits to humanity, he first accepted human service in the body, 136.

God is the Word, 137. God above John, and so forth, 137. Within his bridal chamber he receives only the Virgin, 141. Everything is possible for God. He attends to hearts, not words, 142. The one who is wholly everywhere cannot be held in places, 143. The incarnation of the Word is not an injury to God—and how. In the womb, the Maker of humanity. The greatness of the Virgin’s womb encompassed God, 144. True God from true God, true human being from Mary. When God shines forth, the sight of souls is wounded, 146. God in the flesh is an honor to the creature, not an injury to the Creator, 148. God flees while a human being pursues him, 150. He cannot be ended, 158. God the Father is witness of his Son—why, 160. He is our king, lord, and father, 163. He does not know confinement by time, 167. Why, leaving great things, he loves smaller things, 168. He pursues what was lost in such a way as to retain what he left. He finds what was lost in such a way as not to lose what has been preserved. He contains everything, yet is himself contained by no creature; he confines himself in our body, 170. The immeasurable one surrounds all things, appears, and is seen in places. Why he appears in a bush, a pillar, and a cloud. When God wills, he makes what is human divine, 102. Lavish in giving, he will not be harsh in repaying, 25. God cannot lie. Why he closes or opens eyes, 21. See *Heavenly Father*, *Trinity*.

### God toward human beings

The love of God the Father for his children, 5. See *Heavenly Father*. God’s affection toward evil children returning to him, 5. Piety joined the human being and God, 5. He assumes the role of a shepherd for the benefit of the sheep, 6. He shows mercy while preserving justice. What he gives in place of human mercy, 8. He acts with us so that nothing may perish in the other age, 9. He measures hearts, not hands or places. He freely gives everything we have. He can give little, intending to repay the greatest things, 9. He helps, not in good things, 11. He fasts on our behalf. He descends to us to overcome the devil’s soldiers, 12. He descends from heaven to hell so that there might be a resurrection of the dead, 13.

What kind of God’s love is shown toward the poor, throughout. What is an injury to the poor is God’s honor, 14. The poor person’s food is God’s nourishment. His goodness is directed toward the wicked, 15. Why he came in a human being to human beings. He seeks human beings, not human possessions, 18. He sends scourges on account of our sins, 20. He sleeps when storms attack us. Unchanging in himself, he changes toward us, 23. He promises a hundredfold interest to those who give alms, 25. He receives the poor and does not reject the rich, 28. He is veiled in a human body so that he may not terrify us, 29. He wipes away human wounds, 36. Out of love for the poor he sells the kingdom for a fragment of bread, 41. He asks from a human being only as much as he knows that person possesses. God’s mercy postpones judgment until death, 42. He is debtor to mercy. A human being sins; God turns back—how, 45. He fights for our salvation, 46. In his humanity he displays love, 47. He adapts himself to human limitations in order to save us, 48. Those whom he hates he avoids. He is a parent throughout the ages, 49. By grace he comes to the aid of the weak person because of another’s faith, 50. God returns to sinners if they themselves turn back to him, 20.

God wishes to see in glory the one whom he sees, 54. Seeking the sinner, he seeks not sins but the human being. He seeks the human being amid sins, and for that person’s sake penetrates Tartarus. He does not accept offerings made from another’s possessions. God’s love is known from human generation, 55. God the Father gives everything for salvation. He calls peoples [Col. 1158] through the mouths of priests, 62. God asks us for the Creed so that we may believe. He enables us to see him without seeing him. He seeks to be loved by a human being. He gives life to the dead, salvation to the despairing, and vigor to the stinking, 65. He made creatures for human service, 69. Even angels. He communicated himself to the human being. He tests us when he allows us to go toward the snares of temptations, 70. He lent Christ to the earth so that he might conquer the devil. So that he might be bread, 71. Out of God’s love we were adopted in the womb so that we might be born free, 72. He gives a human being the capacity to perceive divine things, 79, and to think divine thoughts, 81. He smells the holiness of the heart more gratefully than the incense of Arabia, 87. He hastens through the forgiveness of human beings, 90. He hungers for the groans of those who offend and thirsts for sinners’ tears, 93. He compensates for our offense with love, 94. He grants more than is asked, 95.

What he did for humanity from the beginning, 96. He relates the gathering of weeds and wheat to the harvest—how, 97. He calls everyone without distinction of persons, 99. He is a friend to martyrs, 101. He created everything for the sake of humanity, 103. He calls back the souls of the saints, 104. Through Paul he entreats the human being by mercy—why, 108. Through mercy he enlarges the bowels and does other things. He seeks faith, not death. He is appeased by the will, not by killing. A human being pleases God if living well; God is appeased by a sacrifice if it is offered holily, and if it is unblemished; otherwise he is angered, 109. He accepts from a human being what that person can give, 110. He had made nature so that human beings might be created for life, 111. For the greatness of the wound he applied the greatness of the medicine, 113. He bestowed grace on the human being, not on sin. He pours out the rain of piety to erase sins. He seeks the human being solely out of love for humanity, 114. He is an eager investigator of human salvation—how, 121.

In the poor person he cries out to the rich. When despised in the poor person, he does not come to the aid of the rich as a father would, 122. He has provided for everyone’s salvation according to his office, 123. He sets the poor and the rich before one another so that they may in turn be cared for, 124. God appears to the dying for judgment, 125. He demonstrates the form of a human being to human beings so that he may be seen, 131. He gives divine gifts. When he flees from the sinner, he spares him, 21. Unity is acceptable to God, not singularity, 132. The merits of the martyrs are God’s gifts, 135. He took humanity again from a woman’s womb, 143. He is born to restore nature. In ambiguous matters he reveals the truth, 145. By love he invites the world; by fear, the world that is falling, 147. Why he assumed human nature rather than angelic nature. Why he wished to be seen in a human being, 148. God is present where there is no human being to be present, 156. What benefits he gave humanity and what lost things he restored, 161.

God requires our service in human fashion—why. He rebukes those who doubt his promises, 163. Why he sends the doubting believer to the raven. He immediately consoles those whom he rebukes. How much he lowers himself in human fashion. Our Father takes care of us. The one whose life is God cannot die, 166. He receives sinners, whom he sanctifies when he draws near, 168. God is not the receiver of crime but of the human being. He rejoices at the sinner’s return. Love toward us is shown by the fact that, 170. Why he protects like an eagle and a hen. He seeks the wandering sheep like a shepherd. He changes and alters his offices in order to change us for the better. He promises rewards to his laborers. He gave us everything. To the blessed he displays eternal and glorious things, 176.

### Human beings toward God

We enter God’s presence with the heart and through grace, 6. At his sight everything trembles, but the human being rejoices—and why. We owe God the fact that we are born and exist. To deny God what he wants is to will that God deny himself what he desires, 8. Sons of rams are to be brought to God—and who, 10. One’s neighbor must be led to God, even by dragging him, 10. Something must be given to God, 12. The road to God is obstructed by the demon, 16. One reaches God through God. Wealth must be entrusted to God in the poor person so that it may be preserved, 23. One must not be moved from one’s place, 34. He is not defiled by the creature’s touch, 36. He must be publicly praised for benefits received. Sinners flee God, 38. Whoever hears a supplicant opens God’s hearing for himself, 43. That one does not wish to stand before God is the devil’s stealthy theft. Contempt for God makes our times evil. One should rejoice when the true God is known, 46. God’s light is needed in God’s work, 51. He returns to sinners if they themselves turn back to him, 20. God does not accept offerings from another’s possessions, 54. God’s love is known from human generation, 55. The grief of being unable to speak about God is felt, 57. God’s gifts, when returned, are not lost, 59. Those approaching God should be clean in body and soul. One must believe that God exists, 61.

Whoever longs to see God should observe the measure of his vision. A human being cannot comprehend what belongs to God, 62. It is more terrifying that the human being is given to heaven than that God is given to the earth, 67. Yet it is more loving that he has changed the judge into a father. God’s name is either honored by our action or blasphemed, 67. Divine benefits make us afraid, 68. They must be guarded with fear. Whoever believes himself a son of God should correspond to his lineage. A human being cannot comprehend his love, 69. Everything done divinely is to be feared, 70. Fear in speaking with God, 86. If he is great before God, how great will he be among human beings? 88. To be just with God is a divine gift, 89. It is caution to believe humbling things about God slowly, and to feel insults more slowly, 90. Love [Col. 1159] erases the debt owed to God, 94. God is dishonored if his works are explained only in a human fashion, 95. A human being marvels that God is afflicted in a human body, 102. Devotion toward God should be cautious—and why, 109. A human being cannot render anything like the love of God, 110. The human being should be a sinner so that God may be just, 112. Who serves God as much as he has served the world? 114.

Why the human being is a debtor to God. Before God no human being should boast of justice, merit, and so forth, 123. Whoever fears a human being rather than God in legal matters easily deviates from justice, 127. How the human being should follow God rather than precede him, 131. Why the Jew is angered when he sees Christ as God, 131. What must be requested from God, 132. Everything that is feared fears God, 144. How the creature grieved because it could not see God, 147. What love toward God ought to be like. The lover longs to see God. In earthly matters the human being is God’s representative, 148. Whoever goes toward God goes into himself, 152. Whoever makes himself God contradicts the true God, 155. Whoever bears the person of an idol refuses to bear God’s image, 155. To seek God without knowing how to seek him is more a necessity than a guilt, 157. Paul sinned against God through love of God out of ignorance. The profane person does not want God to be born, 158. A human being is bound to serve God alone, 16. Whoever doubts present things while already sensing future things is assigned to the fires of Gehenna, 163. Those who dwell with God do not lack the means of life, 166. The sinner who draws near does not violate God, 168. The bag, bread, and money that we must carry at God’s command, 170. He is invited to dwell in the splendor of the city, temple, and heart, 171. While John reveals the Son of God, he accepts death, 174.

The servants of God stand; they do not lie down, 15. They suffer evil in order to receive crowns.

### Right Hand

The right hand of the Lord is Christ, 33. Virtue is the work of the right hand—how, 9. Christ calls the apostles back to the right hand, 78. Let us flee what belongs to the left if we desire to stand at the right, 9. What it means to pass from the right to the left, 168. See *Left Hand*.

### Devil

The devil, or demon, is the author of despair. What he does to the despairing person and to his hired servant, 2. He would like human beings to become criminals and teachers of crimes, 2. Why he does not allow them to be satisfied. The devil is a liar and a pig, and what he feeds on, 5. He fattens himself on vices. He does not remove hunger. He is the author of evil, and the evil things he does, 11. He tests the beginnings of virtues. He extinguishes good at its very birth. Wicked by himself, more wicked when provoked, 12. He is satiated by faults. He turns food into drunkenness. Who his soldiers are and what they do. He fights by tricks where strength is lacking, 13. He rules over gluttony. He raises a person up in order to cast him down. He seeks one who has fallen. Often defeated, he does not yield. He promises in order to deceive. When he asks to be worshiped, what evils he does. Repulsed by the Lord, he rages against us. Even during Lent—and how. He is the prince of enmities, 14.

He lives in tombs, 16. He delights in burying human beings alive. He suffers evil so that human beings may perish. What frauds he uses when he cannot conquer openly. He ensures that a human being does not return to God, 16. He does not possess a human being unless that person has been withdrawn from divine service. He complains unjustly about time, 16. He changes foul odors. He seeks filth. He is sent into the herd of pigs. Why the pigs die. He wants to destroy everything. He is tormented by human life, thrusts the living into tombs, and places food before the dead, 17. The devil’s guilt redounds to human punishment—and how. Why he promises kingdoms while he himself dwells in tombs, 17. He promises heavenly things in order to drag people toward the lower realms. He uses flattery. He fears and pretends. With a legion, he attacks one person. He is a lazy soldier. He delights in filth and mud. Even pigs cannot endure his odor. The bird of heaven builds its nest and bears fruit, 19.

The devil became such from an angel, 26. His snare is pride. While he promised divine things, he took away human things, 27. His scandal. The devil caused scandal. He is described as a spirit, 52. How he is confined by human senses and is called deaf and mute. The ancient fugitive has besieged human understanding, 52. He deceives human beings so that the evils of the possessed may be believed natural, incurable, or lunatic. He utterly uproots peace, 53. The devil’s robbery placed a human being in a cave, 65. Every evil comes from him, 67. Why the devil is called evil, 70. How he deceives us and drags us into sins, 71. The devil’s temptation is his preliminary servant, 72. He made the world unclean; he dragged the human being to death; and he changed affection into parricide, 96.
